label: First swimming lesson

what_happens.title: What happens at a swimming lesson
goals: The steps: changing room, swimsuit, shower, sit on the edge, into the water with the teacher, games, towel
Kids start in shallow water and hold on to the edge, a float or the teacher
Nobody has to put their face in the water until they are ready
what_happens.parentSkill: Name the steps in order, and say that the teacher stays close in the water.

who_is_there.title: Who is at the swimming lesson
goals: A swim teacher in the water, and a lifeguard who watches everyone
Other kids who are learning too
The grown-up watches from the side or swims too
who_is_there.parentSkill: Tell your child exactly where you will be: in the water or watching from the side.

what_i_do.title: What I do in the pool
goals: Listen to the teacher, hold the edge, kick my legs, blow bubbles
Walk, never run, by the pool
Say "I need a break" when I need one
what_i_do.parentSkill: Practise blowing bubbles and kicking in the bath, and the rule "walk by the pool".

if_scared.title: If the water feels scary
goals: Water can feel cold at first, splashes are loud, the pool smells different
It is okay to go slowly: toes, then legs, then tummy
Calm tools: holding the edge, blowing bubbles, slow breaths, a float
if_scared.parentSkill: Name the feeling and give one small step: 'The water feels big. Let's start with your toes.'

rehearsal.title: Let's practise swimming
goals: Bath-time practice: bubbles, kicking, water on the face with a cup
Say the steps once more, ending with a warm towel
rehearsal.parentSkill: At bath time, practise bubbles and a little water on the forehead, only as far as your child wants.

steps: Change into my swimsuit in the changing room
Walk to the pool and sit on the edge
Get into the water with the teacher
Hold the edge, kick my legs and blow bubbles
Play water games with the other kids
Wrap up in a warm towel and get dressed
sensory: water that feels cold at first, then warmer
a pool smell, like a clean swimming pool
goggles that press a little on the face
water in the ears that sounds like a shell
honestyNotes: Do not promise the child will not go under or get water in the face; say the teacher helps and they can go slowly. Follow the swim school's safety rules. Swimming lessons do not make a child water-safe on their own; always supervise near water.

fallbackAnswer: Kids start where the water is not deep, and they hold on to the edge or a float.
The teacher is right there in the water with you.

questionButtons.text: Do I have to put my face in?
fallbackAnswer: You can start by blowing bubbles with just your mouth.
It can feel cold at first.
After a few kicks, your body gets used to it, and a warm towel waits after.
[[GROWNUP]] watches from the side or swims with you.
You can wave to [[GROWNUP]] any time.
A swim teacher's job is to help kids learn to swim.
They stay close and show you each step.
Yes. Other kids are learning too, and some of them feel nervous too.
You can play the water games together.
If water splashes your face, you can close your eyes, blow out and hold the edge.
The teacher is right there to help you up.
First the changing room and the swimsuit, then a quick shower.
Then you sit on the edge and the teacher helps you in.

techniques.label: Blowing bubbles
techniques.how: Practise blowing bubbles in the bath or a bowl; blowing out keeps water out of the nose.

techniques.label: Holding the edge
techniques.how: Show your child that holding the edge is always allowed and a good place to rest.

techniques.label: Toes first, step by step
techniques.how: Go into the water little by little: toes, ankles, knees, tummy, shoulders.

techniques.label: Bath-time practice
techniques.how: At bath time, practise kicking, floating with support and a little water on the forehead with a cup.

techniques.label: Trying goggles at home
techniques.how: Try goggles at home first so the pressing feeling is familiar.

techniques.label: A wave from the side
techniques.how: Agree a wave signal so your child can see you from the water.

techniques.label: Saying 'I need a break'
techniques.how: Practise saying 'I need a break' and holding the edge to rest.

techniques.label: Smell the flower, blow the candle
techniques.how: Breathe in slowly through the nose like smelling a flower and out like blowing a candle.

techniques.label: Finding a swim buddy
techniques.how: Say hello to one other child at the start and do the games next to them.

ritual: Swimsuit on and a quick shower
Hold the edge, kick and blow bubbles
Warm towel and a wave goodbye

pain: If water gets in your eyes, close them and blink. It stings for a moment.
Say 'I need a break' and hold the edge.
separation: I am right here watching. Wave to me!
I can see you the whole time.
unknown: First the shower, then the edge, then the water with the teacher.
strangers: The swim teacher's job is to help kids learn. They stay close.
Let's say hello to the teacher.
sensory: The water feels cold at first, then your body gets used to it.
Splashes are loud. That is a pool sound.
safety: Hold the edge whenever you like.
Walk, never run, by the pool.
social: The other kids are learning too.
Maybe one of them can be your swim buddy.
body: You put your face in only when you are ready.
Blow bubbles with your mouth first.
love: I am proud of you for trying.
